traits.bark_colour.note: The bark colour chosen by eye for appearance (see its note), as a screen colour: it stood as appearance.bark [0.38, 0.35, 0.31], which is linear light, so the trunk drew pale grey to white beside photographs of the species (2026-10-23). It stands here in sRGB, as bark colours are picked, and the bark rule (tracheophyta) turns it into linear light.

traits.leader.note: Sargent's Manual (sargent-1922, p. 237): open-grown, 'stout branches ... spreading horizontally and forming a broad dense symmetrical round-topped crown' (the leader lost is inferred from the broad round crown).

traits.limb_angle.note: Sargent's Manual (sargent-1922, p. 237): 'stout branches ascending in the forest and forming a narrow spire-like head, or in open positions spreading horizontally and forming a broad dense symmetrical round-topped crown'.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_max_m.note: FEIS's tanoak review (Fryer 2008, read 2026-10-15): "The typical variety is a medium-sized tree, usually attaining 65- to 80-foot (20-24 m) heights"; the champion near Ophir, Oregon, is 43.9 m tall.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: FEIS's tanoak review (Fryer 2008, read 2026-10-15): leaves "sclerophyllous and evergreen, reaching 1 to 5.5 inches (3-14 cm) in length".

traits.leaf_habit.note: FEIS's tanoak review (Fryer 2008, read 2026-10-15): leaves "sclerophyllous and evergreen".

traits.fruit_size_m.note: FEIS's tanoak review (Fryer 2008, read 2026-10-15): "The fruit is an acorn ... ranging from 0.8 to 1.3 inches (2-3 cm) long", usually borne singly but in clusters of 2 to 4.

traits.leaf_width_m.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives a width.

traits.flowering_months.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as the FEIS review read gives no months.

traits.fruiting_months.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as the FEIS review read gives no months.

generator.params.note: Oregon white oak's values, changed by hand for tanoak: ascending branches and a straighter, less forked bole (FEIS, Fryer 2008: "Tanoak boles are generally long and straight", "Branches are ascending"), a broad, rounded open-grown crown a little narrower than the oak's, and smaller leaves. path_half fitted so the tree grows to its reference height. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: Rough sizes: 18 m tall and 45 cm across at breast height at 80 years in the open, below FEIS's usual 20-24 m for mature trees and within its 0.2-0.8 m trunks (Fryer 2008). Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: By eye, after FEIS's description (Fryer 2008): leathery grey-green leaves, oblong and shallowly toothed; erect cream catkins ("spiky catkins"); acorns in shallow cups. Bark grey-brown and furrowed less deeply than the oak's.

generator.params.leaf_years.note: Leaves kept into a second year, as the evergreen leaf habit FEIS gives (Fryer 2008) asks; the review gives no leaf life, so two years by hand, as the built-in evergreen broadleaves mostly keep theirs.

traits.height_typical_m.note: A model estimate (confidence high, record L458543), as no source read gives it.
